    AddSpeakerCategoryItemHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Speakers.UseCases.AddSpeakerCategoryItem · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Speakers/UseCases/AddSpeakerCategoryItem/AddSpeakerCategoryItemHandler.cs:15 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the handler that attaches a category item to a speaker. It is the canonical "load aggregate, call domain method, save, map" template with no extra guards, and it is worth reading first because most write handlers in this module are variations on it.
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>; IUnitOfWork; Result and Error; Speaker and SpeakerCategoryItem; SpeakerCategoryItemDTOMapper; Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.
    • Concept introduced, the load-then-delegate template plus source-generated logging. [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice] assesses whether each write is a thin, self-contained slice: command, validator, and handler sit in one folder and this file is the whole write path. [Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven] assesses the handler contract, here ICommandHandler<AddSpeakerCategoryItemCommand, Result<SpeakerCategoryItemDTO>> (:18). [Rubric §13, Observability & Operability] assesses structured logging: the class is sealed partial so the [LoggerMessage] attribute (:41-42) can generate a strongly typed, allocation-free LogCategoryItemAdded helper whose message template names its parameters, which is what makes the log queryable in App Insights rather than a formatted string.
    • Walkthrough
      • Primary constructor (:15-18): IUnitOfWork, a SpeakerCategoryItemDTOMapper, and ILogger<AddSpeakerCategoryItemHandler>. Note the repository is not injected: it is resolved from the unit of work (:25), which is the framework's rule for keeping one tracked context per scope.
      • HandleAsync (:21) resolves IRepository<Speaker, SpeakerIdentifierType> and loads the aggregate with the include-free overload GetByIdAsync(command.SpeakerId, cancellationToken) (:26). That overload queries the tracked Table deliberately (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/EFReadRepository.cs:154-166), so the entity is change-tracked and the later save is not a silent no-op.
      • A missing speaker returns Error.NotFound decorated with WithSource(...) and WithTarget(...) (:27-28), which is how the API layer later maps a domain failure onto a 404 without the handler knowing about HTTP.
      • It delegates the decision to speaker.AddSpeakerCategoryItem(command.SpeakerCategoryItemId, command.CategoryItemId) (:30); a failed Result is passed straight through with its error list intact (:31-32).
      • On success it saves through the unit of work with ConfigureAwait(false) (:34), logs via the generated helper (:36), and returns Result.Success(dtoMapper.MapToDTO(result.Value!)) (:38).
    • Why it's built this way: pushing "may this category item be added?" into the aggregate keeps the handler as pure orchestration, so the interesting invariant stays unit-testable on Speaker with no database, and the same shape recurs across the module. Returning a Result rather than throwing is the framework-wide error convention (see Group 1).
    • Where it's used: registered by the Conference application DI scan; invoked through the decorator pipeline for SpeakerCategoryItemsController posts (Group 20).
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the aggregate's duplicate check reads its _speakerCategoryItems collection (Speaker.cs:299), but this handler loads the speaker without an explicit include list, so whether that collection is populated depends on the navigation-population behavior described in ADR-002 rather than on anything visible in this file.

    CreateQuestionHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Questions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Questions/UseCases/Create/CreateQuestionHandler.cs:19 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the most interesting handler in this unit. It creates a question, but because question ids are shared with the Sessionize import, it must allocate an id out of a reserved range and cope with a concurrent create that grabs the same one.
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>; IUnitOfWork; IServiceScopeFactory (Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection); IEntityRequestMapper<TEntity, TCreateRequest, TIdentifierType> resolved for QuestionCreateRequestMapper; QuestionDTOMapper; Question and QuestionInvariants; Result and Error.
    • Concept introduced, application-allocated ids in a reserved range with optimistic retry. [Rubric §8, Data Architecture] assesses how identity is assigned when a table is shared between an external system of record and local writes: Sessionize owns the low id space, so user-created questions are allocated from QuestionInvariants.ManualIdRangeStart (999,999,000) to QuestionInvariants.ManualIdRangeEnd (999,999,999) (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Questions/QuestionInvariants.cs:37 and :40). [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity] assesses recovery from a losing race: read-max-then-insert is not atomic, so instead of locking, the handler catches the resulting unique-key violation and retries with a recomputed id. [Rubric §13, Observability & Operability] applies through the two [LoggerMessage] helpers, one informational for the create (:119-120) and one warning that names the attempt number when a collision is retried (:122-123).
    • Walkthrough
      • Primary constructor (:19-24): the unit of work, an IServiceScopeFactory, the request mapper, the DTO mapper, and the logger. MaxManualIdAttempts is a private const int of 3 (:27).
      • HandleAsync (:30) is a while (true) loop over attempts (:38). The first attempt runs CreateCoreAsync against the ambient unit of work (:43-44). Every later attempt opens a fresh DI scope (:48) and resolves a scoped IUnitOfWork from it (:49), because the ambient DbContext still tracks the failed insert and would replay it.
      • The catch filter (:52) is the retry gate: it re-runs only while attempt < MaxManualIdAttempts and IsUniqueKeyViolation(ex) is true. Anything else, including the fourth collision, propagates.
      • CreateCoreAsync (:64) resolves the repository (:69), then reads every existing question inside the reserved range with ignoreQueryFilters: true (:73-77) so a soft-deleted question still reserves its id. nextId is Max(Id) + 1, or the range start when the range is empty (:79-81).
      • Range exhaustion returns a domain-style failure rather than throwing: Error.Failure(nameof(CreateQuestionHandler), "Manual question ID range exhausted.") (:83-84).
      • The caller's id is then unconditionally replaced with a with expression (:87), the request mapper turns the record into a Question (:89), a failed mapping short-circuits (:90-91), and the entity is added and saved (:95-96) before the mapped QuestionDTO is returned (:100).
      • IsUniqueKeyViolation (:108) walks the whole InnerException chain looking for the text "duplicate key", case-insensitively (:110-113). The comment above it states the reason: the Application layer cannot reference EF Core or SQL client types, so detection is message-based and covers both SQL Server errors 2601 and 2627.
    • Why it's built this way: a database identity column is not an option when an external import owns part of the key space, and a pessimistic lock would serialize every question create for a rare conflict. Bounded optimistic retry keeps the common path at one round trip. The message-based exception test is a deliberate trade: it preserves the Clean Architecture dependency rule ([Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]) at the cost of coupling to a provider's error text.
    • Where it's used: registered by the Conference application DI scan and invoked by the pipeline for QuestionsController posts (MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/QuestionsController.cs:33 and :93).
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the catch filter deliberately lets the exception escape once attempts are exhausted, so a sustained collision surfaces as an unhandled exception mapped by the shared exception middleware, not as a Result.Failure. Also, IsUniqueKeyViolation matches on message text, so a non-SQL-Server provider (Cosmos or SQLite under ADR-018) would not necessarily be recognized; nothing in this file pins the provider.

    QuestionCreateRequestMapper

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Questions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Questions/UseCases/Create/QuestionCreateRequestMapper.cs:11 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the adapter that turns a validated QuestionCreateRequest into a Question domain entity by calling the aggregate's static factory.
    • Depends on: IEntityRequestMapper<TEntity, TCreateRequest, TIdentifierType>; Question; Result.
    • Concept introduced, the request mapper as the only door into a factory. [Rubric §4, DDD] assesses whether entities can be constructed in an invalid state: Question.Create (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Questions/Question.cs:70-77) combines the text, entity, type, source, and length invariants and returns a Result<Question>, so a bad request becomes an error list rather than a half-built object. Unlike a DTO mapper, which copies fields outward, a request mapper translates inward and is allowed to fail. Keeping it in its own class means the handler never touches the factory signature, which is what lets CreateQuestionHandler depend on the generic interface instead of the concrete type.
    • Walkthrough: a sealed class with one method, CreateEntityAsync (QuestionCreateRequestMapper.cs:15). It null-guards the request (:17), then returns Task.FromResult(Question.Create(...)) (:19-26): the work is synchronous and the Task exists only to satisfy the async interface. The arguments map one-to-one from the request, with two things worth noticing. QuestionEntity and QuestionType are passed with the null-forgiving operator (:22-23) even though the request declares them nullable, and questionSource is the hard-coded literal "User" (:26), which is what distinguishes an organizer-authored question from an imported one (QuestionInvariants.cs:34 lists the only valid sources as Sessionize and User).
    • Why it's built this way: hard-coding the source at the mapper means the API surface cannot be used to forge a Sessionize-sourced question, and delegating every field check to the factory keeps validation in the domain instead of duplicated in the application layer.
    • Where it's used: resolved by CreateQuestionHandler through the IEntityRequestMapper<Question, QuestionCreateRequest, QuestionIdentifierType> constructor parameter (CreateQuestionHandler.cs:22) and invoked at :89; registered by the module's application service scan.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the ! on the two nullable properties suppresses the compiler warning but does not prevent a null reaching the factory. In that case QuestionInvariants.EnsureQuestionEntityIsValid fails the membership test (QuestionInvariants.cs:68-75) and the call returns a Result.Failure, so the outcome is a validation error rather than a NullReferenceException. That behavior comes from the invariant, not from this file.

    • Depends on: FluentValidation's AbstractValidator<T>; QuestionTextRules<T>.
    • Concept introduced, rule composition with Include. [Rubric §16, Maintainability] assesses whether the same constraint is written once: instead of repeating a required-plus-max-length rule in the create validator and again in the update validator, both Include the generic QuestionTextRules<T>, which is parameterized by a property selector (QuestionCreateRequestValidator.cs:10). [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] applies to the payload the rule set produces: it carries both a human message and a stable machine code (Question.QuestionText.Required, Question.QuestionText.MaxLength, MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Questions/Validation/QuestionValidationRules.cs:17-18), and its length ceiling is QuestionInvariants.QuestionTextMaxLength (1000, MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Questions/QuestionInvariants.cs:13), the same constant the EF configuration uses, so the UI limit and the column width cannot drift apart.

    • Why it's built this way: Include merges the rule set's rules into this validator as though they were declared inline, so composition costs nothing at validation time while keeping one definition of "what a valid question text is".
    • Where it's used: discovered by the module's validator scan and run by ValidatingCommandDecorator<TCommand, TResult> ahead of CreateQuestionHandler.

    SpeakerDTOMapper

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Speakers.DTOs · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Speakers/DTOs/SpeakerDTOMapper.cs:17 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the aggregate-root mapper for Speaker. It composes the two child mappers and, crucially, applies a PII redaction rule: the speaker's email is stripped from the response for anyone who is not an Organizer (BR-66).
    • Depends on: IEntityDTOMapper<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>; Speaker and SpeakerDTO; the child mappers SpeakerCategoryItemDTOMapper and SpeakerQuestionAnswerDTOMapper; ICurrentUserService and RoleNames; the Email value object; Riok.Mapperly's [Mapper] and [UseMapper].
    • Concept introduced, mapper composition with [UseMapper], and authorization-aware projection. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] assesses whether nested contracts map through their own dedicated mappers rather than duplicated inline projections: the two [UseMapper] fields (SpeakerDTOMapper.cs:23-27) tell the generator to route the nested collections through the same mappers the child endpoints use. [Rubric §11, Security] and [Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance] assess whether sensitive fields are withheld at the boundary rather than filtered in the client: this is the one mapper in the family that is not a pure field copy, and it is the last point before serialization where the email can be dropped. The framework's broader PII stance (PiiAttribute, erasure vs soft delete) is ADR-005.
    • Walkthrough
      • The class is [Mapper] sealed partial with a primary constructor taking the two child mappers and ICurrentUserService (:17-21). Each child mapper is stored in a [UseMapper]-annotated private field (:23-27), which is how Mapperly discovers them.
      • MapToDTO (:30) is hand-written, not generated. It null-guards (:32), calls the generated projection MapToDTOGenerated(entity) (:33), and then applies the redaction: currentUserService.IsInRole(RoleNames.Organizer) ? dto : dto with { Email = null } (:36). Because SpeakerDTO is a record class with an init-only nullable Email (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Speakers/SpeakerDTO.cs:9 and :27), the with expression produces a redacted copy without mutating anything.
      • The generated half is the private partial SpeakerDTO MapToDTOGenerated(Speaker entity) declaration (:46). Renaming the public method and keeping a private generated one is the standard Mapperly technique for wrapping generated code with hand-written logic.
      • MapToDTOs (:40-44) projects the collection through the public MapToDTO, so the redaction applies to every element of a list response, not just single-entity reads.
      • NullableEmailToString (:49) is a private static converter the generator picks up to unwrap the Email value object into the DTO's string?.
    • Why it's built this way: enforcing BR-66 in the mapper rather than in each controller means every read path (list, detail, and any nested speaker projection) inherits it, and the with-copy keeps the redaction free of side effects on the entity or on a shared DTO instance.
    • Where it's used: injected into SpeakerEntityQueryService for the speaker read endpoints, into the speaker create and update handlers, and composed via [UseMapper] into the session, event, and speaker-join mappers (SessionSpeakerDTOMapper, EventSpeakerDTOMapper, EventDTOMapper) so nested speaker data is redacted identically.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the redaction depends on ICurrentUserService reflecting the caller. In a background or gRPC context with no user principal, IsInRole returning false yields the redacted (safe) result, but that fallback behavior lives in the auth service, not here.

The [Rubric §4, DDD] point is the sharp one here: the handler never touches a Room. It hands the whole parameter set to Event.UpdateRoom (:31-38), which locates the child through GetRoomOrNotFound, delegates the field updates to room.Update(...), and raises a RoomChanged domain event carrying the event id, room id, and name (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Events/Event.cs:377-388).       • Primary constructor (:13-15): just IUnitOfWork and ILogger<UpdateRoomHandler>. No DTO mapper, because the declared result is Result, not Result<T>.

Both arguments matter: without the include the room would not be in memory for GetRoomOrNotFound to find, and without tracking the mutation would not be picked up by SaveChangesAsync.

    • Concept introduced, the command that declares its own transaction. [Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven] assesses whether a write is modeled as an explicit single-purpose message: this record carries intent only, and the two marker interfaces tell the pipeline how to run it. [Rubric §10, Cross-Cutting] assesses whether such concerns are declared rather than hand-coded: implementing ITransactional (:13) opts the message into TransactionalCommandDecorator<TCommand, TResult>, and the XML comment states the reason plainly (:7-8): the Speaker link and the outbox row that carries the cross-context User update must commit together or not at all. Implementing ICacheInvalidating with CachePrefix => $"{typeof(Speaker).FullName}:" (:16) is what makes CachingCommandDecorator<TCommand, TResult> drop every cached read keyed under the Speaker type after a successful link.
    • Walkthrough: a sealed record with a two-parameter positional constructor (:13) and one member, the expression-bodied CachePrefix (:15-16). The cross-module identifier pairing is the notable part: UserIdentifierType is Identity's alias, carried here as a plain scalar because the two modules own separate databases and there is no foreign key to point at (ADR-006).
    • Why it's built this way: the two markers move durability and cache eviction out of the handler and into the pipeline, so LinkUserToSpeakerHandler reads as pure domain orchestration. Records give value equality and immutability for free.
    • Where it's used: constructed by SpeakersController's PUT /Speakers/{id}/link action from a LinkUserRequest body (Group 20, MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SpeakersController.cs:346, handler injected at :49); handled by LinkUserToSpeakerHandler.

Marking it ICacheInvalidating (:10, :13) means a successful create evicts the cached speaker reads exactly like the command records above.

Id (:16) is a SpeakerIdentifierType, and its comment records that it is Sessionize-assigned: the caller supplies the key rather than the database generating it, which is what lets an import be idempotent. The same is true of the four profile-link members, which the mapper also drops (Email, by contrast, IS forwarded). Nothing on this type says so.

    UserRegisteredHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Users.IntegrationEventHandlers · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Users/IntegrationEventHandlers/UserRegisteredHandler.cs:40 · Level 8 · class

    • What it is: the Conference-side subscriber to Identity's UserRegistered integration event. When someone registers an account, this handler tries to find the speaker profile that belongs to them and links the two automatically (BR-207). It is the most security-sensitive type in this unit, and the most instructive: nearly every design decision in it was made in response to a specific failure.
    • Depends on: IIntegrationEventHandler<in TIntegrationEvent> closed over UserRegistered; IServiceScopeFactory (Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection); IUnitOfWork and IRepository<TEntity, TIdentifierType>; IEventBus; Speaker and SpeakerLinkedToUser; the Email value object; Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.
    • Concept introduced, the singleton event handler that opens its own scope. [Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven] assesses whether cross-module reactions are event-driven rather than direct calls: Identity never references Conference, it publishes, and this class reacts. [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] assesses whether that reaction survives a process split: it does, because delivery is the broker's job (locally RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus in production) and this handler only sees the event object. The lifetime detail is the teachable one. Integration event handlers are registered as singletons by the framework scan (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:125-129), but IUnitOfWork is scoped, so a singleton cannot take it in its constructor. The handler therefore injects IServiceScopeFactory (:41) and creates one await using scope per event (:51) from which it resolves the unit of work and the event bus (:52-53). The class comment states this convention explicitly (:36-38).
    • Concept introduced, refusing to trust attacker-controlled input as an identity proof. [Rubric §11, Security] assesses whether an automated privilege grant is based on something the requester cannot forge. There is now exactly ONE match strategy, email equality (:14-15). A name-based fallback used to run whenever the email match missed, which covered Sessionize-imported speakers (the public view/All endpoint omits PII, so their Email is always null). It was removed as a security fix, and the comment spells out why (:18-24): first and last name arrive straight from the registration form and prove nothing, so anyone who knew a speaker's name could register under it and take over that speaker profile. Email-less speakers are now linked deliberately by an organizer through PUT /Speakers/{id}/link (see LinkUserToSpeakerCommand).
    • Walkthrough
      • HandleAsync (:45) null-guards the event (:47), then does all of its work inside the per-event scope. It resolves IRepository<Speaker, SpeakerIdentifierType> from the unit of work (:55) rather than injecting it, which is the framework rule for keeping one tracked context per scope.
      • TryMatchByEmailAsync (:130) builds an Email value object from the event payload and logs-and-bails when the address is malformed (:137-142). It then queries speakers with where: s => s.Email != null && s.Email == emailVO and asTracking: true (:145-149); tracking is required because the match is about to be mutated. The comment at :135-136 records why the comparison is safe: Email normalizes to lowercase on creation and EF stores the normalized value, so direct equality is effectively case-insensitive.
      • The result ordering is deliberate and worth reading twice: .OrderBy(s => s.LinkedUserId.HasValue).ThenBy(s => s.Id).FirstOrDefault() (:154-157). When an email is shared by two speaker rows, an arbitrary FirstOrDefault could pick an already-linked record, abandon the link, and then pick a different one on a retry. Preferring unlinked and then ordering by id makes the choice deterministic across attempts.
      • On a miss, LogNameMatchCandidatesAsync (:167) runs. This is a read-only organizer cue, not a fallback: it counts unlinked speakers whose first and last name equal the registration's (:183-187) and logs the count (:191). The matched rows are never returned, so no code path can link on a name. The comment (:180-182) notes that SQL Server's default SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS collation makes the equality case-insensitive, and that the global soft-delete query filter excludes deleted rows automatically.
      • Three guards precede the link. A speaker already linked to a different user is left alone (:66-70). A speaker already linked to this user re-publishes SpeakerLinkedToUser so Identity can re-sync, then returns without re-linking (:74-80), which makes redelivery idempotent. A failing speaker.LinkUser(...) is logged and abandoned (:82-87).
      • The happy path saves through the unit of work (:92) and then publishes SpeakerLinkedToUser on IEventBus (:95-97) so Identity populates User.LinkedSpeakerId.
      • LogAndRethrow (:124) is an exception filter, not a catch body: it logs and returns false, so the exception keeps propagating and the catch block at :101-105 is unreachable (the code says so at :103). The remarks explain the fix (:111-122): the handler used to swallow everything, which meant one transient database fault lost the auto-link permanently, because the delivery was already acked and nothing retried. Letting the exception through hands the decision to the delivery mechanism, which is built for it: the outbox retries to its limit and then dead-letters, and MassTransit redelivers and then moves the message to the error queue. Retrying is safe because the unique-index race it can lose resolves on the next attempt through the "already linked to a different user" guard.
      • Seven [LoggerMessage] partial methods (:195-214) cover every branch, which is what makes the auto-link auditable after the fact.
    • Why it's built this way: ADC deliberately uses an integration event here where Store uses an in-process domain event for the same concept, because Identity and Conference are separate services with separate databases (ADR-006, ADR-003). The auto-link is therefore eventually consistent, and the class comment is explicit about the user-visible consequence (:29-34): a brand-new user's first token does not yet carry the speaker_id claim, it appears on the next refresh, and the 5-minute output cache refreshes on expiry rather than being invalidated from here, because invalidating would require an AspNetCore dependency the Application layer must not take.
    • Where it's used: registered as a singleton by the framework's integration-handler scan reached through ScanModuleApplicationServices<ClassReference>() (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:106), and wired to the broker in the Conference service host by RegisterIntegrationEventConsumer<UserRegistered>() (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:320-321), which attaches the generic IntegrationEventConsumer<TEvent> adapter. When MessageBus:Provider is unset the transport falls back to in-process, which is how integration tests boot the host without a broker (Program.cs:318-319).
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the unique-index race on Speaker.LinkedUserId is described in a comment (:89-91) but the index itself is defined in the Infrastructure EF configuration, not here.

    EventLiveValidationService

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Events · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Events/EventLiveValidationService.cs:18 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the Conference-side implementation of IEventLiveValidationService, the narrow contract Engagement's conference-day live layer calls to learn whether an event or session is live and who is allowed to act on it.
    • Depends on: IEventLiveValidationService (the interface, which lives in Conference.Shared so consumers need no reference to this assembly); IUnitOfWork; the Event and Session aggregates; SessionInvariants; CurrentEventSelector; the EventLiveInfo and SessionLiveInfo payloads; Result and Error.
    • Concept introduced, a cross-module read contract implemented in the owning module. [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] assesses whether cross-module dependencies flow through interfaces a process boundary can later intercept. Engagement owns the live experience but not the source of truth for events and sessions, so it asks Conference through this interface. In-process (tests, single-host runs) the DI container binds it to this class (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:102); across processes the same interface is satisfied by EventLiveValidationServiceGrpcAdapter and served by a gRPC endpoint, and Engagement's code does not change (ADR-007). When Conference is disabled entirely, the module registers DisabledEventLiveValidationService instead (MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/ConferenceModule.cs:24). [Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]: everything here runs over repository abstractions, with no EF or transport type in sight.
    • Walkthrough
      • GetEventLiveInfoAsync (:21) resolves the Event repository from the unit of work (:25) and loads untracked with an empty include list (:26-30), returns Error.NotFound decorated with source and target when the event is missing (:32-36), and otherwise returns an EventLiveInfo carrying the published flag and the computed UTC window (:38-40).
      • GetSessionLiveInfoAsync (:44) loads the session with includes: [nameof(Session.SessionSpeakers)] (:49-53), because the caller needs the speaker list to decide presenter rights (BR-236).
      • It then enforces the same eligibility rules the bookmark path uses, by calling the domain's own invariants rather than restating them: SessionInvariants.EnsureNotServiceSession (BR-91, :63) and SessionInvariants.EnsureStatusIsEligible (BR-49, :67). A failure is converted into a typed failure with the domain's error list intact (:64-69).
      • The parent event is loaded next (:71-76) with the same not-found treatment (:78-82), the window is computed (:84), and the active speaker ids are projected with the soft-deleted joins filtered out: [.. session.SessionSpeakers.Where(ss => !ss.IsDeleted).Select(ss => ss.SpeakerId)] (:86-87).
      • The returned SessionLiveInfo (:89-96) carries the event id, the published flag, the window, the speaker ids, IsPlenumSession, and the event's QuestionModerationDefault (BR-233), so one call answers every question the live layer has.
      • ComputeLiveWindowUtc (:102-106) is a three-line delegation to CurrentEventSelector.GetLiveWindowUtc, and the comment above it says why (:99-101): the window rule, the unknown-zone degradation, and the spring-forward-gap guard must stay identical to the ones the home surfaces and the now-next snapshot use. The rule itself lives in Conference.Shared (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Events/CurrentEventSelector.cs:64-83): the window opens at StartDate 00:00 local and closes, exclusive, at EndDate + 1 day 00:00 local, converted from the event's IANA zone, degrading to treating the local dates as UTC when the zone id is unknown.
    • Why it's built this way: centralizing "is this live and eligible" behind one interface, and reusing the domain invariants and the shared window math instead of copying them, gives both modules one authoritative answer. See ADR-007 for the extraction rationale.
    • Where it's used: registered scoped at MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:102; consumed by Engagement's live layer (LivePolls and SessionQuestions), reaching this class over gRPC in production.

    LinkUserToSpeakerHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Speakers.UseCases.LinkUser · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Speakers/UseCases/LinkUser/LinkUserToSpeakerHandler.cs:20 · Level 9 · class

    • What it is: the handler for LinkUserToSpeakerCommand. It updates the Conference side of a bidirectional link that spans two databases, and raises the event that updates the other side.
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>; IUnitOfWork; Speaker; SpeakerLinkedToUser; Result and Error; Microsoft.Extensions.Logging. Note what is not injected: there is no publisher service, because the event is raised on the aggregate.
    • Concept introduced, cross-context coordination captured in the same transaction. [Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven] and [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]. Conference and Identity own separate databases (ADR-006), so there is no foreign key between Speaker and User and consistency has to flow through events. The load-bearing detail is the ordering: speaker.AddDomainEvent(new SpeakerLinkedToUser(...)) runs BEFORE the single SaveChangesAsync (:54, then :56), so the outbox row is written inside the same transaction as the link (ADR-003). The class comment states the failure this removed (:14-18): with a post-save publish, a crash could commit the Conference-side link and lose the event that sets User.LinkedSpeakerId. The OutboxProcessor later routes the row to the registered IMessageBus transport. This is also why the command carries ITransactional.

      • Primary constructor (:20-22): IUnitOfWork and ILogger<LinkUserToSpeakerHandler>; the declared result is the non-generic Result, so no DTO mapper is needed.
      • HandleAsync (:25) resolves the repository (:29) and loads the speaker with the include-free, tracked overload (:30), returning Error.NotFound with source and target set when it is missing (:31-32).
      • The BR-208 uniqueness guard (:34-46) is the interesting part: it queries every speaker whose LinkedUserId equals the target user (:35-38) and fails with Error.Invariant(code: "Speaker.UserAlreadyLinked", ...) if any other speaker already holds that link (:39-46). The s.Id != command.SpeakerId test is what makes re-linking the same pair a no-op rather than an error.
      • speaker.LinkUser(command.UserId) (:48) is the domain decision. The aggregate refuses a speaker that is already linked, returning Speaker.AlreadyLinked (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Speakers/Speaker.cs:253-262), so the handler owns only the cross-row rule and the entity owns its own.
      • On success it raises the integration event on the aggregate (:54), saves (:56), and logs through the generated LogUserLinkedToSpeaker (:58, declared :64-65). The domain Result is returned either way (:61), so a rejection reaches the API with its error codes intact.
    • Why it's built this way: splitting the rules (uniqueness across speakers in the handler, "already linked?" inside the aggregate) keeps each check where the data for it lives, and the pre-save event raise is a deliberate durability fix rather than a style choice.
    • Where it's used: registered by the Conference application scan; invoked through the decorator pipeline by SpeakersController's link action (Group 20, SpeakersController.cs:345-347). The emitted event is consumed on the Identity side to set User.LinkedSpeakerId.

    • Caveats / not-in-source: only the two names are validated here. Email is left entirely to the Email value object inside Speaker.Create, so a malformed address arrives as an invariant failure rather than a field-level validation error.

Identical mechanism to LinkUserToSpeakerHandler: the event goes onto the aggregate before the single SaveChangesAsync, so the outbox row commits with the unlink (ADR-003), and the class comment repeats the crash scenario it removes (:13-17). The aggregate refuses an unlinked speaker with Speaker.NotLinked (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Speakers/Speaker.cs:271-280), so by the time the success branch runs, previousUserId is guaranteed to have had a value; the HasValue guard at :40 is belt and braces.

    • What it is: the handler that creates a speaker. It is deliberately the thinnest handler in this unit: map, add, save, project. Compare it with the session and question create handlers, which need reserved id ranges and collision retries; a speaker id is a client-assigned GUID, so none of that machinery is required here.

    • Concept reinforced, the generic create slice end to end. [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]: the request IS the command, so the class implements ICommandHandler<SpeakerCreateRequest, Result<SpeakerDTO>> (:20) and the four types of the slice sit in one folder. [Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]: the handler orchestrates a mapper, a repository, and a DTO mapper without embedding any construction logic of its own. [Rubric §11, Security] reaches it indirectly through the response: SpeakerDTOMapper redacts the speaker's email for non-organizers (BR-66), so even the create response obeys the same rule as every read.

      • Primary constructor (:16-20): unit of work, the request mapper resolved by its generic interface, the DTO mapper as a concrete type, and ILogger<CreateSpeakerHandler>.

    • Why it's built this way: validation, cache invalidation, and transaction scope are all handled by the pipeline decorators wrapped around this handler (declared by the markers on SpeakerCreateRequest), which is exactly why the create logic can reduce to four statements.
    • Where it's used: registered by the Conference application scan; dispatched by SpeakersController's POST /Speakers through the base controller (MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SpeakersController.cs:46 and :284-291), and by the Sessionize import path, which supplies the Sessionize GUID as Id.

    EventNavigationPopulator

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Events · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Events/EventNavigationPopulator.cs:11 · Level 10 · class

    • What it is: the declarative navigation populator for the Event aggregate. It loads the three child collections the framework's read path cannot materialize through .Include() on this model.
    • Depends on: DeclarativeNavigationPopulator<TEntity> (the base); ChildNavigationDescriptor<TEntity, TParentId, TChild, TChildId>; IUnitOfWork; the Event, Room, EventSpeaker, and EventQuestionAnswer entities.
    • Concept introduced, declarative child loading instead of imperative joins. [Rubric §2, Design Patterns] assesses whether repetition is factored into a reusable abstraction: rather than write load-and-assign code, this class passes a list of descriptors to its base constructor (:13-36), each naming the property, the parent-key selector, the child foreign-key selector, and an assign action. The base runs the loads and the assignments uniformly; the class body is literally empty (:37-38). [Rubric §8, Data Architecture]: adding a child collection is one descriptor, not a new query method. The mechanism and its rationale are taught in Group 11 and ADR-002.
    • Walkthrough: three descriptors, all keyed on Event.Id against the child's EventId. Rooms assigned through SetRooms (:15-21), EventSpeakers through SetEventSpeakers (:22-28), and EventQuestionAnswers through SetEventQuestionAnswers (:29-35). The AssignAction targets are worth a look: all three Set* methods are internal on the aggregate (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Events/Event.cs:460, :556, :633), reachable from here only because the Domain project grants <InternalsVisibleTo Include="MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application" /> (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain.csproj:3). Hydration therefore goes through the domain's own guarded mutators while staying closed to every other assembly.
    • Why it's built this way: an aggregate that exposed public collection setters would be mutable by anyone; an aggregate with no setters at all could not be hydrated. The internal plus InternalsVisibleTo pairing gives the populator exactly the access it needs and nobody else any (ADR-002).
    • Where it's used: registered as INavigationPopulator<Event> (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:52) and resolved by the read pipeline whenever an Event is loaded with these navigations requested.

    AddSessionCategoryItemCommand

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.AddSessionCategoryItem · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/AddSessionCategoryItem/AddSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:10 · Level 9 · record

    • What it is: the command to attach a category item (a track, a level, a room-type tag) to an existing session. It is a three-field positional record: the owning SessionId, an optional SessionCategoryItemId for the join entity, and the CategoryItemId being associated (AddSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:10-13).
    • Depends on: ICacheInvalidating (the pipeline marker it implements), the Session domain type (used only for its FullName when building the cache prefix), and the SessionIdentifierType / SessionCategoryItemIdentifierType / CategoryItemIdentifierType module aliases (ADR-048).
    • Concept introduced, the nullable child id on an Add command: the second parameter is SessionCategoryItemIdentifierType?, documented as "explicit ID for the join entity, or null for database-generated identity" (AddSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:8). The REST path always passes null and lets the database assign the key (SessionCategoryItemsController at MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SessionCategoryItemsController.cs:193); the parameter exists so an importer that already knows the id can supply it, which is the same shape the aggregate's AddSessionCategoryItem factory call takes (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/Session.cs:408-410). [Rubric §9, API and Contract Design] assesses whether a contract states exactly what a caller may decide: making the id nullable rather than defaulted keeps "let the database choose" distinct from "I chose zero".
    • Walkthrough: the record body holds one member, CachePrefix => $"{typeof(Session).FullName}:" (AddSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:15-16). That satisfies ICacheInvalidating, so the Caching decorator evicts every cache entry under the Session prefix after the command succeeds, outside the transaction (the decorator order is fixed by ADR-014). All session reads key under that same prefix, so adding a category item flushes the session projections in one stroke rather than requiring per-query bookkeeping.
    • Why it's built this way: caching and invalidation are declared by the message and applied uniformly by the pipeline (ADR-026), never hand-wired inside a handler. [Rubric §10, Cross-Cutting]: the command says what it invalidates; it does not know how.
    • Where it's used: validated by AddSessionCategoryItemCommandValidator, handled by AddSessionCategoryItemHandler, and constructed by the POST /SessionCategoryItems endpoint (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SessionCategoryItemsController.cs:187-193).

    PublicSessionStatusSpecification

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.Specifications · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/Specifications/PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:20 · Level 9 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the BR-49 public-visibility status allow-list, written once as an EF-translatable predicate. A session is publicly visible when its Status is unset or equals Accepted: s => s.Status == null || s.Status == SessionStatuses.Accepted (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:23-24). Organizer-created sessions never carry a status, which is why null is on the allow-list (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:8-9).

    • Depends on: the framework base Specification<TEntity, TIdentifierType> closed over Session / SessionIdentifierType (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:20), the domain catalog SessionStatuses, and System.Linq.Expressions (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:1).

    • Concept introduced, restating a domain rule as an expression tree so it survives translation: [Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design] assesses whether business rules live in the model with one authoritative statement each, and [Rubric §8, Data Architecture] assesses whether queries stay engine-portable. The rule already exists in the domain as SessionStatuses.IsEligible(status) (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/SessionStatuses.cs:54-56), and that is what the write side and the bookmark guard call. A LINQ provider cannot translate a compiled method call, so a read filter that invoked IsEligible would either fail to translate or quietly pull every session into memory first. This class is the read-side twin of the same allow-list, expressed as an Expression<Func<Session, bool>> the provider renders into a WHERE. The remarks state that intent and record the one behavioral difference (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:12-18): IsEligible compares with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase (SessionStatuses.cs:54-56), while the expression uses ==, so it is SQL Server's case-insensitive collation, not the C# operator, that makes the two agree on a differently cased value.

    • Walkthrough: two members, and the split between them is the whole design.

      • StatusCriteria (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:22-24) is a public static readonly Expression<Func<Session, bool>>. It is exposed on its own because callers compose it into a larger expression rather than evaluating it: it is handed to CrossSourceSpecification.BuildAsync as the local predicate, which rebinds it onto the foreign-key selector's parameter and ANDs it in, so the combined predicate stays translatable.
      • Criteria (PublicSessionStatusSpecification.cs:26-27) is the override the base requires and simply returns StatusCriteria, so an instance works anywhere the framework takes a Specification<TEntity, TIdentifierType>, including AndSpecification<TEntity, TIdentifierType> composition and the base's in-memory IsSatisfiedBy path.

      One rule, two entry points, no second copy of the predicate.

    • Why it's built this way: keeping the criteria free of navigation properties (no s.Event.IsPublished) is an enforced convention, not a preference. SpecificationConventionTests fails the build for any specification that filters by navigating to another entity, because such a predicate stops translating the moment that entity moves to a different data source; the rule and its rationale are stated at MMCA.ADC/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.ADC.Architecture.Tests/SpecificationConventionTests.cs:3-11, which also records that ADC's entities all route to SQL Server today and the guard is a forward safeguard (ADR-018, ADR-015). The published-event half of public visibility therefore never appears here; the caller ANDs it in as a resolved id list.

    • Where it's used: the public-visibility slice. GetPublicSessionFilterHandler passes StatusCriteria as the local predicate of its cross-source build, and PublicConferenceVisibility uses both forms: the expression for GetVisibleSessionIdsAsync and an instance for its private eligible-session resolver, ANDed with an event-scope specification.

    • Caveats / not-in-source: there is no dedicated test class for this type; it is exercised through the GetPublic*FilterHandler test classes under MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Tests/. The collation claim in the remarks is a statement about the deployed database, not something this file can enforce.

    SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.DTOs · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/DTOs/SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:12 · Level 9 · class (sealed partial)

    • What it is: the entity-to-DTO mapper for the SessionCategoryItem join entity. It is a Mapperly source-generated mapper: the class declares the signature, the generator writes the body at compile time.
    • Depends on: IEntityDTOMapper<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> closed over SessionCategoryItem / SessionCategoryItemDTO / SessionCategoryItemIdentifierType (SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:13), and the Riok.Mapperly.Abstractions package for the [Mapper] attribute (SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:4, SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:11).
    • Concept introduced, compile-time mapping instead of runtime reflection: [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability] assesses whether hot per-row work avoids reflection, and [Rubric §15, Best Practices] assesses whether generated code is preferred to hand-maintained boilerplate that can silently drift. [Mapper] on a partial class makes Mapperly emit the body of public partial SessionCategoryItemDTO MapToDTO(SessionCategoryItem entity) (SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:15-16) as plain property assignments in a generated file. There is no runtime configuration step and no reflection at map time; a property that cannot be matched is a build diagnostic, not a null at runtime. This is the "manual mapping over reflective auto-mapping" position of ADR-001, taken one step further: the compiler writes the manual mapping.
    • Walkthrough: two members.
      • MapToDTO (SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:15-16) is partial with no body; the generator supplies it.
      • MapToDTOs (SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper.cs:18-23) is written by hand: null-guard, then a collection-expression spread over Select(MapToDTO). Its body is identical to the default interface implementation on the contract (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/IEntityDTOMapper.cs:27-32); re-declaring it on the class is what makes it callable through the concrete type, which matters because the handlers in this unit inject the concrete mapper (AddSessionCategoryItemHandler.cs:18) rather than the interface.
    • Why it's built this way: DTO shaping stays a compile-checked, allocation-lean step owned by the Application layer, so the API contract cannot drift from the entity without a build error (ADR-001).
    • Where it's used: injected into AddSessionCategoryItemHandler (AddSessionCategoryItemHandler.cs:18), composed into SessionDTOMapper for the parent's child collection, and resolved by the generic EntityQueryService registered for this entity (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:90). It is registered by the convention scan at DependencyInjection.cs:106, not by an explicit line.

The Validating decorator sits between Caching and Transactional in the command pipeline and runs every registered validator for the command type before the transaction opens (ADR-014), so a malformed command costs no database work. Because the identifier alias is a value type, default is the "not supplied" sentinel that model binding produces for a missing JSON field, so this rule is what turns a silently omitted field into a 400 rather than a lookup miss deeper in.

      • Only on success does it SaveChangesAsync with ConfigureAwait(false) (ADR-049), log, and return Result.Success(dtoMapper.MapToDTO(result.Value!)) (AddSessionCategoryItemHandler.cs:35-39). The new child is mapped from the value the aggregate returned, not re-queried.

    • Where it's used: registered by the convention scan (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:106) and injected into SessionCategoryItemsController as ICommandHandler<AddSessionCategoryItemCommand, Result<SessionCategoryItemDTO>> (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SessionCategoryItemsController.cs:49). Covered by AddSessionCategoryItemHandlerTests.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: unlike its two siblings, this handler uses the id-only overload, which loads no includes, so the aggregate's duplicate check (Session.cs:412) evaluates against whatever SessionCategoryItems the context happens to have materialized rather than against a freshly loaded collection. The filtered unique index on (SessionId, CategoryItemId) is the database backstop for a duplicate that gets past it (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/SessionCategoryItemConfiguration.cs:30-32). Whether that asymmetry with AddSessionSpeakerHandler is intentional is not determinable from source: no comment states it.

    AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.AddSessionQuestionAnswer · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/AddSessionQuestionAnswer/AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:19 · Level 10 · class (sealed partial)

    • What it is: the richest write path in this unit. Where the other two Add handlers are three-step orchestrations, this one runs a chain of five business rules before it decides between creating a new answer and updating the caller's existing one (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:13-18 names them: BR-91, BR-49, BR-108, BR-128, BR-124, BR-107).
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>, IUnitOfWork, ICurrentUserService, SessionQuestionAnswerDTOMapper, the Session, Event, and Question aggregates with their invariant helpers (SessionInvariants, EventInvariants, QuestionInvariants), Result / Error, and logging (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:1-9, AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:19-23).
    • Concept introduced, an application-level upsert over an aggregate, and where its race is caught: [Rubric §6, CQRS and Event-Driven] assesses whether a command slice owns its full decision, and [Rubric §8, Data Architecture] assesses whether integrity rules have a database-level guarantee and not only an in-memory one. BR-107 says one live answer per (session, question, author), so the handler looks for an existing non-deleted answer of the current user for this question in the already loaded child collection (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:50-52) and branches: found means update, not found means create (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:54-57). That check is in-memory by construction, so two concurrent submissions can both take the create branch. The database is the backstop, and the entity configuration says so in as many words: a filtered unique index on (SessionId, QuestionId, CreatedBy) stops the second write and the shared DbUpdateException handler turns it into a 409 (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/SessionQuestionAnswerConfiguration.cs:39-45). Reading the handler alone would leave you thinking the rule is best-effort; reading the pair shows the real guarantee.
    • Walkthrough: the primary constructor adds ICurrentUserService to the usual three dependencies (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:19-23).
      • HandleAsync (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:26-58) loads the session with its SessionQuestionAnswers and asTracking: true (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:31-35), because both the upsert lookup and the subsequent mutation need the children tracked. A missing session is Error.NotFound (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:36-37).
      • ValidateSessionEligibilityAsync (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:60-81) reuses domain invariants rather than restating them: SessionInvariants.EnsureNotServiceSession (BR-91, a break or a lunch slot takes no feedback, :65), SessionInvariants.EnsureStatusIsEligible (BR-49, the same allow-list PublicSessionStatusSpecification expresses for reads, :70), then a load of the parent Event and EventInvariants.EnsureEventIsPublished (BR-108, :75-80). Each check short-circuits on failure.
      • ValidateQuestionAsync (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:83-102) loads the Question and rejects a question that does not exist or whose QuestionEntity is not "Session" with a validation error coded Question.NotFoundOrWrongEntity (BR-128, :88-97), then hands the answer text to QuestionInvariants.EnsureAnswerValueMatchesQuestionType (BR-124, :100-101).
      • UpdateExistingAnswerAsync (:104-117) calls session.UpdateSessionQuestionAnswer(existingAnswer.Id, command.AnswerValue), saves, and maps the same tracked instance back out, so the response carries the new value.
      • CreateNewAnswerAsync (:119-131) calls session.AddSessionQuestionAnswer(...) and maps the child the aggregate returned. Both branches emit the same log line (:133-134), so the log does not distinguish an insert from an update.
    • Why it's built this way: the eligibility rules are shared with other callers (the bookmark validation service and the live-info service call the same SessionInvariants helpers), so the handler composes rules instead of copying conditions, and every check returns a Result that folds into the same failure channel (ADR-013). [Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]: cross-aggregate reads go through IUnitOfWork repositories, never EF types.
    • Where it's used: injected into SessionQuestionAnswersController (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SessionQuestionAnswersController.cs:58), whose whole surface requires an authenticated caller (SessionQuestionAnswersController.cs:55). Covered by AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandlerTests.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: currentUserService.UserId!.Value (AddSessionQuestionAnswerHandler.cs:50) is null-forgiving. Nothing inside this handler enforces that a user id is present; the guarantee comes from the controller's RequireAuthenticated policy (SessionQuestionAnswersController.cs:55), so a caller reaching this code with no id would fault rather than fail gracefully. The three validation helpers each issue their own round-trip (session, event, question), which is four reads before any write on the create path.

That matters because the aggregate's duplicate rule is evaluated over the in-memory collection: _sessionSpeakers.Exists(ss => !ss.IsDeleted && ss.SpeakerId == speakerId) (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/Session.cs:316). Loading the collection is therefore part of satisfying the invariant, not an optimization. asTracking: true is required because the include overload defaults to no-tracking (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/EFReadRepository.cs:169-182), and an untracked aggregate would make the subsequent save a silent no-op. [Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design] and [Rubric §8, Data Architecture]: the load shape is chosen by what the aggregate must decide, and the filtered unique index on (SessionId, SpeakerId) still backs it at the database level (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/SessionSpeakerConfiguration.cs:30-32).
    • Walkthrough: primary constructor with unitOfWork, dtoMapper, and a typed ILogger (AddSessionSpeakerHandler.cs:16-19). HandleAsync (AddSessionSpeakerHandler.cs:22-40) loads as above, returns Error.NotFound for a missing session (:28-29), delegates to session.AddSessionSpeaker(command.SessionSpeakerId, command.SpeakerId) (:31), forwards a domain failure unchanged (:32-33), then saves, logs through the generated LogSpeakerAddedToSession (:35-37, :42-43), and returns the mapped join row (:39). The aggregate raises SessionSpeakerChanged as part of the add (Session.cs:333), which the outbox picks up in SaveChangesAsync (ADR-003).

Covered by AddSessionSpeakerHandlerTests.

    SessionDTOMapper

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.DTOs · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/DTOs/SessionDTOMapper.cs:14 · Level 10 · class (sealed partial)

    • What it is: the mapper for the Session aggregate itself, and the one place in this unit where the three child mappers are composed. It maps a session and, in the same pass, its speakers, question answers, and category items.
    • Depends on: IEntityDTOMapper<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> closed over Session / SessionDTO / SessionIdentifierType (SessionDTOMapper.cs:18), and the three sibling mappers SessionSpeakerDTOMapper, SessionQuestionAnswerDTOMapper, and SessionCategoryItemDTOMapper, taken as primary-constructor parameters (SessionDTOMapper.cs:14-17).
    • Concept introduced, mapper composition with [UseMapper]: each injected mapper is stored in a private field annotated [UseMapper] (SessionDTOMapper.cs:20-27). That attribute tells the Mapperly generator: when you need to map a SessionSpeaker to a SessionSpeakerDTO while filling this type, call that mapper instead of generating a second, private copy of the same mapping. The payoff is that SessionDTO's three child collections (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Shared/Sessions/SessionDTO.cs:66-72) are filled by exactly the same code the child endpoints use, so a session read and a GET /SessionSpeakers read can never disagree about a child's shape. [Rubric §2, Design Patterns]: composition over duplication, expressed declaratively. [Rubric §16, Maintainability]: adding a field to a child DTO is one edit, not four.
    • Walkthrough: three [UseMapper] fields assigned from the primary constructor (SessionDTOMapper.cs:20-27), the generator-supplied public partial SessionDTO MapToDTO(Session entity) (SessionDTOMapper.cs:29-30), and the same hand-written MapToDTOs collection method the siblings carry (SessionDTOMapper.cs:32-37). Note the dependency direction: this type is Level 10 precisely because it depends on the three Level 9 mappers.
    • Why it's built this way: children are mapped by their owners' mappers, so the DTO graph is assembled from single-purpose pieces the DI container already has (ADR-001). What the child collections actually contain at map time is decided earlier, by the navigation populators (ADR-002): this mapper copies what was loaded and never triggers a query itself.
    • Where it's used: injected into CreateSessionHandler and UpdateSessionHandler for the write-path response DTO, and resolved as IEntityDTOMapper<Session, SessionDTO, SessionIdentifierType> by the generic EntityQueryService registered for sessions (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:57), which is what every session read endpoint goes through (ADR-034). Registration is by the convention scan at DependencyInjection.cs:106.

    GetNowNextQuery

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.NowNext · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/NowNext/GetNowNextQuery.cs:23 · Level 9 · record

    • What it is: the query object for the "happening now / up next" snapshot behind the home-screen widget (ADR-042 Wave 8). It carries one nullable parameter, EventId (GetNowNextQuery.cs:23); a value targets a specific published event, and null tells the handler to auto-select the current-or-next published event, which is what the home widget passes because it has no event id of its own (GetNowNextQuery.cs:8-12).
    • Depends on: IQueryCacheable (the marker it implements), the Session domain type (used only for its FullName when building the cache key), the EventIdentifierType module alias, and the BCL CultureInfo/TimeSpan.
    • Concept introduced, query-level read caching: this is the first type in this unit to implement IQueryCacheable, the read side of the caching decorator taught in the CQRS pipeline. A query that implements it is intercepted by the caching decorator, which reads or writes a cache entry keyed on CacheKey for CacheDuration before the handler runs. [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability] assesses whether hot reads avoid recomputation and database round-trips: here a public, non-user-specific read that the home surface hits on every load is memoized instead of recomputed. [Rubric §10, Cross-Cutting]: caching is a pipeline concern the query only declares, never implements.
    • Walkthrough: CacheKey (GetNowNextQuery.cs:26-35) composes "{Session.FullName}:NowNext:{scope}", where scope is the invariant-culture event id or the literal "current" when EventId is null (GetNowNextQuery.cs:30-33). Placing the key under the Session full-name prefix is deliberate: the session write commands in this unit invalidate on that same prefix (see RemoveSessionCategoryItemCommand), so any session mutation evicts this snapshot once an IConnectionMultiplexer is registered. CacheDuration (GetNowNextQuery.cs:38) is a deliberately short 30 seconds; the XML remarks state why (GetNowNextQuery.cs:16-19): it bounds staleness both from event-level edits and from the continuous now/next time-bucket transitions, and it is the sole backstop when prefix eviction is unavailable.
    • Why it's built this way: keying under the aggregate prefix lets one prefix eviction cover every derived read of that aggregate, and the short TTL keeps a time-sensitive widget honest even without a cache server. See the caching-decorator rationale in the CQRS pipeline.
    • Where it's used: handled by GetNowNextHandler; dispatched from the Conference now-next read endpoint and the home-screen widget.

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.RemoveSessionCategoryItem · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/RemoveSessionCategoryItem/RemoveSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:9 · Level 9 · record

    • What it is: the command to detach a category-item association from a session. It is a two-field sealed record, SessionId plus the join-entity id SessionCategoryItemId (RemoveSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:9-11).

A command that implements it declares a CachePrefix; after the command succeeds, the invalidation decorator evicts every cache entry whose key starts with that prefix. CachePrefix => $"{typeof(Session).FullName}:" (RemoveSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:14) is the same prefix the session reads key under (including GetNowNextQuery), so removing a category item flushes all cached session projections in one stroke. [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability] and [Rubric §10, Cross-Cutting]: read caching and its invalidation are declared by the messages and applied uniformly by the pipeline, never hand-wired per handler.
    • Walkthrough: the record body is only the CachePrefix expression-bodied property (RemoveSessionCategoryItemCommand.cs:13-14); the two ids are positional parameters.

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/Create/SessionCreateRequest.cs:10 · Level 9 · record

    • What it is: the create request DTO for a conference session. It doubles as the create command itself: CreateSessionHandler is declared as ICommandHandler<SessionCreateRequest, Result<SessionDTO>> (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/Create/CreateSessionHandler.cs:27), so the request travels the CQRS pipeline unchanged.

Title (SessionCreateRequest.cs:19) and EventId (SessionCreateRequest.cs:61) are required; everything else is optional, including the schedule (StartsAt/EndsAt, SessionCreateRequest.cs:25-28), status and lifecycle flags (Status, IsInformed, IsConfirmed, IsServiceSession, IsPlenumSession, SessionCreateRequest.cs:31-43), the URL and info fields (LiveUrl, RecordingUrl, AccessibilityInfo, ResourceLinks, SessionCreateRequest.cs:46-55), Duration (SessionCreateRequest.cs:58), and the assigned RoomId (SessionCreateRequest.cs:64). Id (SessionCreateRequest.cs:16) is caller-supplied but auto-generated when left at its default (see CreateSessionHandler for the manual-id logic). CachePrefix returns the Session full-name prefix (SessionCreateRequest.cs:13), matching the read caches and the other session write commands.

[Rubric §9, API and Contract Design]: the contract is a small, explicit, immutable shape. [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice]: request, validator, mapper, and handler all live in the one UseCases/Create folder.

IsInformed, IsConfirmed, and Duration are accepted on the request but are not forwarded by the mapper (see SessionCreateRequestMapper).

    ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Categories · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Categories/ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator.cs:11 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the navigation populator for the Category aggregate. It loads the one child collection (CategoryItem) that EF Core cannot materialize through .Include() on this model (ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator.cs:7-9). It is the simplest populator in the Conference module: a single descriptor and an empty class body.
    • Depends on: DeclarativeNavigationPopulator<TEntity> (the base it extends, closed over Category), ChildNavigationDescriptor<TEntity, TParentId, TChild, TChildId> (the descriptor shape), IUnitOfWork (passed straight through to the base), and the Category/CategoryItem entities.
    • Concept reinforced, declarative child loading over hand-written joins: the mechanism is taught in Group 11 (ADR-002); the job here is pure binding. The subclass supplies data, not an override: the base constructor takes the IUnitOfWork plus a collection-expression array of descriptors (ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator.cs:11-22) and owns the bulk fetch-and-assign algorithm. [Rubric §2, Design Patterns]: Template Method configured by data rather than by virtual methods. [Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]: the Application layer describes hydration with repository abstractions and property selectors, with no EF Core namespace anywhere in the file.
    • Walkthrough: one ChildNavigationDescriptor<Category, ConferenceCategoryIdentifierType, CategoryItem, CategoryItemIdentifierType> (ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator.cs:15) with four settings: PropertyName = nameof(Category.CategoryItems) (:17), ParentKeySelector = e => e.Id (:18), ChildForeignKeySelector = child => child.CategoryId (:19), and AssignAction = (e, categoryItems) => e.SetCategoryItems(categoryItems) (:20). The assign action goes through the aggregate's own SetCategoryItems mutator rather than a back-door property setter, so hydration respects the same guard rails a business operation would. Note the parent-key type: the Conference module's category alias is ConferenceCategoryIdentifierType, not a bare CategoryIdentifierType, because the module also has category items and shares the workspace-wide alias convention (see primer).
    • Why it's built this way: one descriptor per collection means adding a child navigation is a data edit, not a new query method, and every aggregate in the module hydrates through the same code path (ADR-002).
    • Where it's used: registered as the INavigationPopulator<Category> implementation by the Conference Application module registration, services.TryAddScoped<INavigationPopulator<Category>, ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator>() (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:64), and resolved by the navigation-population pipeline whenever a Category is read with CategoryItems requested.

    GetNowNextHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.NowNext · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/NowNext/GetNowNextHandler.cs:20 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the handler that builds the now-next snapshot: the sessions running at the query instant plus the next starting batch, for one published event or the auto-selected current-or-next event (GetNowNextHandler.cs:12-19).
    • Depends on: IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TResult>, GetNowNextQuery, IUnitOfWork, the Event and Session aggregates, CurrentEventSelector (event auto-selection and live-window math), CalendarExportMapper (eligibility plus wall-clock-to-UTC conversion), the NowNextDTO and NowNextSessionDTO shapes, Result, and the BCL TimeProvider.
    • Concept introduced, a TimeProvider-injected clock for a time-bucketed read: the handler takes TimeProvider timeProvider in its primary constructor (GetNowNextHandler.cs:20-22) and reads GetUtcNow() once (GetNowNextHandler.cs:29), so "now" is a single injected, testable instant rather than an ambient DateTime.UtcNow sampled repeatedly through the method. [Rubric §14, Testability]: a fake TimeProvider lets a test place the wall clock precisely inside or across a session boundary. [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]: pairing this handler with the 30-second cache on its query keeps a per-load widget cheap.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Selects the event via SelectEventAsync (GetNowNextHandler.cs:90-113): an explicit id loads that event with its Rooms (GetNowNextHandler.cs:96-101); a null id loads all published events and defers to CurrentEventSelector.SelectCurrentOrNext (GetNowNextHandler.cs:107-112). A missing or unpublished event returns Error.NotFound (GetNowNextHandler.cs:32-36).
      • Loads the event's sessions, builds a room-id to name map, and resolves the IANA time zone, falling back to TimeZoneInfo.Utc on TimeZoneNotFoundException (GetNowNextHandler.cs:38-51).
      • Filters sessions through CalendarExportMapper.IsExportable and projects each to a row carrying both the local and the UTC start/end via CalendarExportMapper.ToUtc (GetNowNextHandler.cs:53-56, GetNowNextHandler.cs:80-88).
      • "Now" is the rows whose [StartsAtUtc, EndsAtUtc) interval contains the instant, ordered by start then room name with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase (GetNowNextHandler.cs:58-62). "Next" is the batch sharing the earliest future start, so parallel tracks surface together rather than one arbitrary winner (GetNowNextHandler.cs:64-72).
      • Computes the event's live flag from CurrentEventSelector.GetLiveWindowUtc and returns a NowNextDTO (GetNowNextHandler.cs:74-77).
    • Why it's built this way: reusing the calendar-export eligibility and DST conversion keeps the now-next view consistent with the exported schedule (one rule, two readers), and the earliest-future-start batching matches how attendees think about "up next" across concurrent tracks (ADR-042 Wave 8).
    • Where it's used: dispatched behind the Conference now-next endpoint and the home-screen widget.

    PublicConferenceVisibility

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Common · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Common/PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:28 · Level 10 · class (static)

    • What it is: the one definition of "what may an anonymous or non-privileged caller read from the conference catalog", expressed as three id-list resolvers. Callers turn the returned lists into Id IN (...) specifications, so closing a visibility leak in this file closes it on every public read at once (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:10-15).
    • Depends on: IUnitOfWork (read repositories only), the Event, Session, and SessionSpeaker entities, PublicSessionStatusSpecification (the BR-49 status allow-list), CrossSourceSpecification, AndSpecification<TEntity, TIdentifierType>, and InlineSpecification<TEntity, TIdentifierType>.
    • Concept introduced, authorization-by-id-list instead of authorization-by-join: the three rules are stated in the remarks (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:17-21): an event is visible when published (BR-108); a session is visible when its event is visible AND its status is on the BR-49 allow-list; a speaker is visible when they have at least one eligible session inside the scoped published-event set (BR-239). Every rule is resolved as a scalar id projection, never as a navigation join such as s.Event.IsPublished (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:22-26). Three things follow: the criteria stay translatable on any engine (the polyglot safeguard of ADR-018), each aggregate keeps a by-id boundary to the others so a future extraction can answer the same question over a service call, and the resulting specifications pass the architecture fitness test that bans navigation-property filters. [Rubric §11, Security] assesses whether authorization is centralized and fail-closed: this class is a single choke point, and every "nothing visible" path returns an empty list, which the callers render as an IN () that matches no rows rather than as an unfiltered read. [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] and [Rubric §8, Data Architecture]: id lists cross an aggregate boundary; joins do not.
    • Walkthrough: three public resolvers plus one private helper, and the ordering between them is the rule hierarchy.
      • GetPublishedEventIdsAsync (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:36-47) projects e.Id where e.IsPublished, untracked (:42), then materializes once so callers embed a stable collection EF can translate into an IN (:45-46). That materialize-once comment is load-bearing: re-enumerating a lazy sequence inside an expression tree is what makes such a filter fail to translate.
      • GetVisibleSessionIdsAsync (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:56-77) builds the event scoping through CrossSourceSpecification.BuildAsync, passing principalPredicate: e => e.IsPublished, dependentForeignKey: s => s.EventId, and localPredicate: PublicSessionStatusSpecification.StatusCriteria (:62-69), then projects the matching session ids (:71-74). It uses the same helper and the same criteria the public session read filter uses, so a session hidden from the session list can never stay reachable through a speaker or junction read (:60-61).
      • GetVisibleSpeakerIdsAsync (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:99-127) takes an optional eventId scope. With a scope, the published-event set is narrowed to that one id, and an unpublished or unknown scoped event narrows it to empty rather than raising an error (:108-112), which is the fail-closed reading of BR-108. An empty scope, or an empty eligible-session set, short-circuits to [] (:114-119). Otherwise it projects the distinct SpeakerId values off the SessionSpeaker join for those sessions (:121-126). The remarks record a real leak this shape fixed (:92-98): the EventSpeaker join is deliberately NOT consulted, because the Sessionize import writes a row there for every speaker in the response, so reading it as a visibility grant published the whole imported roster and made the filter vacuous. The session link is the only acceptance signal a speaker carries.
      • GetEligibleSessionIdsAsync (PublicConferenceVisibility.cs:134-151) is the private variant used by the speaker rule, which needs to narrow an already resolved event scope. It ANDs a PublicSessionStatusSpecification instance with an InlineSpecification over the scoped id list (:141-143), which keeps the criteria a translatable IN filter with no navigation join, and reuses the one status allow-list rather than restating it.
    • Why it's built this way: a single shared definition is the only way five independent read handlers can agree on what "public" means. The two entry points into PublicSessionStatusSpecification (the raw StatusCriteria expression for composition, an instance for specification algebra) exist precisely so this class can use whichever form each call site needs without a second copy of the predicate.
    • Where it's used: five public-read handlers call it: GetPublicSessionSpeakerFilterHandler (GetPublicSessionSpeakerFilterHandler.cs:24), GetPublicSessionCategoryItemFilterHandler (GetPublicSessionCategoryItemFilterHandler.cs:25), GetPublicSpeakerFilterHandler (GetPublicSpeakerFilterHandler.cs:26), GetPublicSpeakerCategoryItemFilterHandler (GetPublicSpeakerCategoryItemFilterHandler.cs:26), and GetPublicEventSpeakerFilterHandler, which calls two of the three resolvers (GetPublicEventSpeakerFilterHandler.cs:31, :38). All five live under MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the class is static and takes its IUnitOfWork per call, so it is not injectable and cannot be substituted in a test; callers are tested against it directly. Cost is another thing the source does not hide: the speaker rule issues up to three sequential round-trips (events, sessions, join rows), which is the price of avoiding a cross-aggregate join.
