    SessionCreateRequestMapper

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/Create/SessionCreateRequestMapper.cs:11 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the adapter that turns a validated SessionCreateRequest into a Session domain entity by calling the aggregate's Create factory (SessionCreateRequestMapper.cs:7-9).
    • Depends on: IEntityRequestMapper<TEntity, TCreateRequest, TIdentifierType> (the framework contract it implements, closed over Session/SessionCreateRequest/SessionIdentifierType, SessionCreateRequestMapper.cs:11-12), the Session factory, and Result.
    • Concept introduced, request-to-entity mapping as its own step: the create pipeline separates "shape the input" (this mapper) from "orchestrate the use case" (the handler). CreateEntityAsync (SessionCreateRequestMapper.cs:15-34) guards the null request with ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull (:17), then forwards the request fields positionally into Session.Create(...) (:19-33), returning that factory's Result<Session> wrapped in an already-completed Task. There is no async here at all: the mapping is synchronous, and the Task exists only to satisfy the interface, which other entities implement with genuinely asynchronous lookups. [Rubric §1, SOLID]: single responsibility, the mapper knows the factory's argument order and nothing else. [Rubric §2, Design Patterns]: the mapper decouples the request DTO from the domain constructor so the handler depends only on the interface and never on this class. Manual mapping over reflection-based mapping follows ADR-001.
    • Walkthrough: fourteen positional arguments, in factory order: Id, Title, Description, StartsAt, EndsAt, Status, IsServiceSession, IsPlenumSession, LiveUrl, RecordingUrl, AccessibilityInfo, ResourceLinks, EventId, RoomId (SessionCreateRequestMapper.cs:20-33). Three request fields are deliberately absent from that list: IsInformed, IsConfirmed, and Duration are accepted on SessionCreateRequest but never reach Session.Create, so the factory's own defaults win for those on a create.
    • Where it's used: injected into CreateSessionHandler as IEntityRequestMapper<Session, SessionCreateRequest, SessionIdentifierType>, so the handler is constructed against the interface and this class is only named at registration.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: whether the three unmapped fields are an intentional "set them on update, not on create" policy or an oversight is not stated in this file or in the factory's documentation.

    SessionCreateRequestValidator

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/Create/SessionCreateRequestValidator.cs:7 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the FluentValidation validator for SessionCreateRequest. It composes reusable per-field rule sets rather than restating each rule inline (SessionCreateRequestValidator.cs:6).
    • Depends on: FluentValidation (AbstractValidator<T> and its Include) and the shared Session*Rules<T> classes from MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.Validation (SessionCreateRequestValidator.cs:1-2).
    • Concept introduced, composed validation via reusable rule includes: the constructor (SessionCreateRequestValidator.cs:9-19) calls Include(...) once per field rule set, each rule class generic over the request type and constructed with a property selector, for example Include(new SessionTitleRules<SessionCreateRequest>(p => p.Title)) (:11). Include folds the other validator's rules into this one, so the composite reports a single flat error list. Because the rule classes are generic over the request type rather than tied to one DTO, the create and update requests can share the identical rule instance shape. [Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety] and [Rubric §15, Best Practices and Code Quality]: a rule such as title length or URL format is defined once, so it cannot drift between the create and update paths. The validator runs in the CQRS pipeline before the handler executes.

Note what is not validated here: StartsAt/EndsAt ordering and the room assignment are enforced further in, by the domain factory and by CreateSessionHandler's BR-130 room check, because both need data this validator does not have.

    CreateSessionHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Sessions.UseCases.Create · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/UseCases/Create/CreateSessionHandler.cs:22 · Level 11 · class (sealed partial)

    • What it is: the command handler for creating a session, and the richest write path in this group. It assigns manual ids in a reserved range, validates the room assignment (BR-130 cross-event plus double-booking), delegates entity construction to the mapper, persists, maps the result to a DTO, and retries on a concurrent id collision (CreateSessionHandler.cs:15-21).
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult>, IUnitOfWork, IEntityRequestMapper<TEntity, TCreateRequest, TIdentifierType> (satisfied by SessionCreateRequestMapper), SessionDTOMapper, the Session and Event aggregates, SessionInvariants (the reserved manual-id range), SessionRoomScheduling (the BR-130 room rules), the SessionDTO result shape, Result, plus IServiceScopeFactory and logging (CreateSessionHandler.cs:22-27).
    • Concept introduced, application-assigned ids with a bounded retry on collision: session ids are application-assigned because the int primary key IS the Sessionize id (CreateSessionHandler.cs:76-78). When the caller supplies no id (organizer create, where the request Id defaults to 0), CreateCoreAsync reads every existing row inside the reserved manual range with ignoreQueryFilters: true so soft-deleted rows still reserve their id, then takes Max(Id) + 1 or the range start when the range is empty (CreateSessionHandler.cs:79-89); an exhausted range returns a failure rather than wrapping around (CreateSessionHandler.cs:91-92). That range is SessionInvariants.ManualIdRangeStart = 999,999,000 through ManualIdRangeEnd = 999,999,999 (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/SessionInvariants.cs:41, :44), deliberately above any real Sessionize id. Because two concurrent creates can compute the same next id, HandleAsync wraps the attempt in a bounded loop of MaxManualIdAttempts = 3 (CreateSessionHandler.cs:30, CreateSessionHandler.cs:42-62); a duplicate-key failure recomputes the id in a fresh DI scope via scopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope() so a clean DbContext is used, since the ambient one still tracks the failed insert (CreateSessionHandler.cs:51-55). [Rubric §8, Data Architecture]: id allocation is an explicit, range-partitioned concern rather than a database identity column, which is what lets an imported id and a hand-created id share one table. [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]: the collision path is exceptional and capped at three attempts, not a lock on the hot path.
    • Walkthrough:
      • An explicit caller id (a Sessionize import, for example) is respected as-is and gets a single attempt with no id recomputation, because a collision there is a genuine caller error (CreateSessionHandler.cs:37-40).
      • CreateCoreAsync (CreateSessionHandler.cs:69-136) takes the unit of work as a parameter rather than closing over the injected one, which is exactly what makes the fresh-scope retry possible. It resolves the manual id when unset and rewrites the request with a with expression (CreateSessionHandler.cs:94).
      • The room rules run only when RoomId has a value (CreateSessionHandler.cs:100): the parent event is loaded untracked with its Rooms (:102-107, Error.NotFound when missing at :108-109), then SessionRoomScheduling.ValidateRoomAssignmentAsync checks that the room belongs to this event (BR-130, error code Session.RoomId.CrossEvent) and that the [StartsAt, EndsAt) slot does not overlap another session in the same room (:111-121, with excludeSessionId: null because nothing exists yet to exclude). The comment at :97-99 explains why the event load is inside this branch: a room-less session has nothing to validate and create has no other use for the event.
      • It then maps via requestMapper.CreateEntityAsync with an early return on failure, adds, saves, logs, and returns Result.Success(dtoMapper.MapToDTO(entity)) (CreateSessionHandler.cs:124-135).
      • IsUniqueKeyViolation (CreateSessionHandler.cs:143-152) walks the whole exception chain looking for the text "duplicate key", case-insensitively. Detection is message-based because the Application layer cannot reference EF Core or SQL Server types, and both SQL Server errors 2601 and 2627 carry that wording (CreateSessionHandler.cs:138-142).
    • Why it's built this way: keeping organizer-created ids in a reserved high range prevents them from colliding with future Sessionize-assigned ids, and the fresh-scope retry is the only reliable way to recover from a duplicate-key race without leaking EF types into the Application layer. The double-booking half of the room check is documented in SessionRoomScheduling as a deliberate SOFT guard: probe and insert are separate statements, so two concurrent organizer writes can both pass it, accepted because the endpoint is organizer-only and the outcome is repairable (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Sessions/Validation/SessionRoomScheduling.cs:16-25). Structured logging uses the source-generated [LoggerMessage] partials LogSessionCreated and LogManualIdCollision (CreateSessionHandler.cs:154-158), the collision one at Warning level so a retry storm is visible in telemetry.
    • Where it's used: registered as the handler for SessionCreateRequest; invoked from the session create endpoint and from the Sessionize import path.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the manual-id scan loads every row in the reserved range to compute a maximum rather than projecting one scalar, so its cost grows with the number of hand-created sessions; nothing in the file bounds that. Message-based exception matching is also locale-sensitive by nature, and the code notes only the SQL Server error numbers, not what a different provider would report.

    DeleteEventHandler

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Events.UseCases.Delete · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Events/UseCases/Delete/DeleteEventHandler.cs:16 · Level 10 · class (sealed partial)

    • What it is: the one delete in the Conference module that is not the framework's generic handler. Deleting an Event must also soft-delete every Session that belongs to it, and a session is a separate aggregate the event cannot reach, so this handler loads both graphs and hands them to a domain service (DeleteEventHandler.cs:11-15 states exactly that rationale: BR-127 for the session cascade, BR-72 for the event's own children).
    • Depends on: ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TResult> closed over DeleteEntityCommand<TEntity, TIdentifierType><Event, EventIdentifierType> and Result (DeleteEventHandler.cs:19), IUnitOfWork, IEventCascadeDeletionDomainService (implemented by EventCascadeDeletionDomainService), the Event and Session aggregates, Error, and Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (DeleteEventHandler.cs:1-7).
    • Concept introduced, replacing a generic framework handler by registering a more specific one: [Rubric §2, Design Patterns] assesses whether a general mechanism can be specialized without being forked, and [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice] assesses whether one use case can deviate without disturbing its neighbours. The framework ships DeleteEntityHandler<TEntity, TIdentifierType>, which loads one entity by id, calls Delete(), and saves (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/UseCases/DeleteEntityHandler.cs:21-35). Sessions, Speakers, Categories, and Questions all take that generic registration; Event alone is bound to this class instead (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:54 versus :58, :62, :66, :71). Because both implement the same closed interface, ICommandHandler<DeleteEntityCommand<Event, EventIdentifierType>, Result>, the substitution is invisible above: EventsController takes that interface in its constructor (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/EventsController.cs:50) and passes it straight to the AggregateRootEntityControllerBase<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType, TCreateRequest> delete slot (EventsController.cs:57-58). No route, no request shape, and no other slice changes.
    • Concept introduced, the include list is what makes an in-memory cascade work: [Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design] assesses whether the aggregate stays the owner of its own invariants. Event.Delete() soft-deletes the event and then walks its three owned child lists in memory (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Events/Event.cs:280-311), and Session.Delete() does the same over its three (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Sessions/Session.cs:271-302). A child that was never materialized is a child the loop cannot see. That is why the includes arrays on DeleteEventHandler.cs:29 (Rooms, EventSpeakers, EventQuestionAnswers) and DeleteEventHandler.cs:38 (SessionSpeakers, SessionQuestionAnswers, SessionCategoryItems) match the collections those two Delete() overrides iterate, one for one. They are not there to shape a response: this handler returns a bare Result with no payload. asTracking: true on both loads (DeleteEventHandler.cs:30, :40) is equally load-bearing, since an untracked graph would make the subsequent save a silent no-op.
    • Walkthrough: a primary constructor taking unitOfWork, eventCascadeDeletionDomainService, and a typed ILogger (DeleteEventHandler.cs:16-19).
      • HandleAsync (DeleteEventHandler.cs:22-52) resolves the write repository through IUnitOfWork rather than injecting one (DeleteEventHandler.cs:26) and loads the event with its owned children (:27-31). A missing event returns Error.NotFound stamped with source and target (:32-33), the standard failure shape of the Result pattern (ADR-013).
      • The second read is the cross-aggregate half: the Session repository's GetAllAsync with the child includes and the predicate s => s.EventId.Equals(entity.Id) && !s.IsDeleted (:36-41). EventId is a plain scalar column on Session, not a navigation, which is what lets this stay a single translatable query.
      • eventCascadeDeletionDomainService.CascadeDelete(entity, sessions) (:44) is the only decision point. The implementation deletes each session first and returns the first failure unchanged, only then deleting the event (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Services/EventCascadeDeletionDomainService.cs:16-30), so a refused session delete leaves the event untouched.
      • Only on success does the handler call unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken) and log (:45-49); the failure path returns without saving (:51), discarding the in-memory mutations the aborted cascade already applied.
      • LogEventDeleted is a source-generated [LoggerMessage] partial method (:54-55), which is why the class is partial. [Rubric §13, Observability and Operability]: the log line is emitted once, after the save, with the event id as a structured field.
    • Why it's built this way: the split is deliberate. What cascades is a business rule, so it lives in a pure domain service with no infrastructure dependencies (EventCascadeDeletionDomainService.cs:7-12); which rows to load is an application concern, so it lives here. Atomicity comes from one SaveChangesAsync covering both aggregates: they are entities of the same module and therefore the same ADC_Conference database (ADR-006), so EF wraps the whole cascade in a single transaction. The domain events each Delete() raised (EventChanged with DomainEntityState.Deleted at Event.cs:307, SessionChanged at Session.cs:298) are captured into the outbox in the same save (ADR-003). Soft-delete, not erasure, is the workspace default: Delete() sets IsDeleted and the context's named SoftDelete query filter hides the rows from every later read (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/DbContexts/ApplicationDbContext.cs:255).
    • Where it's used: registered as the Event delete handler at MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:54 and reached through DELETE /Events/{id} on EventsController, which requires the EventsManage permission at the controller level (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/EventsController.cs:43, ADR-020) and overrides DeleteAsync to evict three output-cache tags afterwards, conference:events, conference:sessions, and conference:rooms, because the cascade invalidates all three read surfaces (EventsController.cs:352-365). Covered by DeleteEventHandlerTests (MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Tests/Events/UseCases/DeleteEventHandlerTests.cs:15), which mocks both repositories and the domain service.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: DeleteEntityCommand<TEntity, TIdentifierType> implements ICacheInvalidating only, not ITransactional (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/UseCases/DeleteEntityCommand.cs:11), so the Transactional decorator does not wrap this handler (ADR-014); the single SaveChangesAsync is the whole atomicity story. The !s.IsDeleted clause on :39 restates what the global soft-delete filter already enforces, since the repository only bypasses filters when ignoreQueryFilters is set and this call leaves it at its default (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/EFReadRepository.cs:26-40). The save uses ConfigureAwait(false) (:47) while the two reads do not; CA2007 is switched off repo-wide in ADC (MMCA.ADC/.editorconfig:348), so nothing enforces either choice here. Finally, the session load is unpaged: an event with a very large session count loads every session and its children into memory in one batch, and no source comment records a ceiling for that.

    SpeakerEntityQueryService

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Speakers · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Speakers/SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:15 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the only per-entity read service the Conference module writes by hand. It is a five-line subclass of the framework's generic EntityQueryService<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> whose entire contribution is one dictionary entry: the DTO field FullName maps to the entity expression (FirstName + " " + LastName) (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:28-31).
    • Depends on: the base EntityQueryService<TEntity, TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> closed over Speaker / SpeakerDTO / SpeakerIdentifierType (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:21-22), and the five constructor dependencies it forwards: IUnitOfWork, INavigationMetadataProvider, IEntityQueryPipeline, SpeakerDTOMapper, and INavigationPopulator<in TEntity><Speaker> (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:15-20). Note that the mapper parameter is the concrete SpeakerDTOMapper, narrowed from the base's IEntityDTOMapper<...> parameter.
    • Concept introduced, a server-authored property map as the bridge between a DTO contract and a queryable column: [Rubric §9, API and Contract Design] assesses whether the public sort and filter vocabulary is stable and independent of the storage model, and [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability] assesses whether that vocabulary still resolves to server-side SQL rather than in-memory work. Speaker.FullName is a computed C# property (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Speakers/Speaker.cs:54) that is explicitly not mapped to a column (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Infrastructure/Persistence/EntityConfiguration/SpeakerConfiguration.cs:67-68 calls builder.Ignore(p => p.FullName)). A client that asks to sort by FullName is therefore asking for something the database has no column for. The map turns that request into a dynamic-LINQ fragment the provider can render: QueryFieldService.ApplySorting looks the name up, and on a hit passes the mapped string straight into query.OrderBy(...) as "(FirstName + \" \" + LastName) ascending" (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/QueryFieldService.cs:144-153); the filter path resolves the same entry before applying its strategy (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/Filtering/QueryFilterService.cs:84-97). The result is one ORDER BY over concatenated columns instead of a page fetched and re-ordered in the host.
    • Concept introduced, why a map hit is trusted: [Rubric §11, Security] assesses whether client-supplied strings can widen what a query touches. Validation runs before the pipeline and accepts a map hit unconditionally, without reflecting over the mapped value, precisely because map values are server-authored and are deliberately not plain property names (QueryFieldService.cs:260-296 documents the rule; the base wires it at MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/EntityQueryService.cs:223-228). A name with no map entry has to resolve to a real public property of the entity or the sort falls back to the default instead of reaching Dynamic LINQ (QueryFieldService.cs:119-148). So the trust boundary is the class you are reading: whatever a subclass puts in this dictionary is executed as a query fragment, which is exactly why the dictionary is private static readonly and not configurable from outside.
    • Walkthrough: three things happen, and that is the whole file.
      • The primary constructor takes the five services and forwards them unchanged to the base (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:15-22). No field is kept; nothing is overridden about how a query executes.
      • PropertyMap is a private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> with the single FullName entry (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:28-31), built once at class load rather than per request.
      • DTOToEntityPropertyMap => PropertyMap (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:34) overrides the base's protected virtual hook, whose default is an empty case-insensitive dictionary (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/EntityQueryService.cs:56-61). The base then threads that map into both validation (EntityQueryService.cs:225-227) and the query parameters handed to the pipeline (EntityQueryService.cs:425-437).
    • Why it's built this way: subclassing is the registration hook. Every other Conference read is served by the closed generic registered directly, for example EntityQueryService<SpeakerCategoryItem, SpeakerCategoryItemDTO, ...> at MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:96; only Speaker needs a non-default map, so only Speaker gets a named subclass, registered as IEntityQueryService<Speaker, SpeakerDTO, SpeakerIdentifierType> at DependencyInjection.cs:61. That keeps ADR-034's generic read layer intact: the specialization is additive data, not a second query implementation. [Rubric §1, SOLID]: the base is open for extension through one protected member and closed to modification.
    • Where it's used: injected into SpeakersController as IEntityQueryService<Speaker, SpeakerDTO, SpeakerIdentifierType> (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.API/Controllers/SpeakersController.cs:45), which is what serves the list and detail speaker endpoints. The map is not theoretical: the speaker list page sorts by "FullName" ascending on every fetch and turns its search box into a ("contains", term) filter on the same field (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Speaker/SpeakerList.razor.cs:145, :158, the SpeakerList page's sortable, filterable FullName column at SpeakerList.razor:100). Covered by SpeakerEntityQueryServiceTests (MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Tests/Speakers/SpeakerEntityQueryServiceTests.cs:15), which pins the exact expression string as a constant (:17) so a silent edit fails the build.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the mapped expression assumes both name parts are non-null strings; SQL Server's concatenation semantics, not this class, decide what a null part renders as. The base's default map is case-insensitive (EntityQueryService.cs:61) while this override supplies a plain Dictionary with the default comparer (SpeakerEntityQueryService.cs:28), so lookups of fullname or FULLNAME miss the map here; a miss then falls back to reflecting FullName on the entity, which does exist (Speaker.cs:54), so the filter path still resolves but the sort would order by a property EF cannot translate. No test in the repository exercises a differently cased sort column, so the runtime outcome of that path is not determinable from source.

    SpeakerNavigationPopulator

    MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Speakers · MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/Speakers/SpeakerNavigationPopulator.cs:11 · Level 10 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the Speaker aggregate's declaration of which child collections have to be loaded by hand when EF Core cannot Include() them. The class has an empty body: everything it says is said in the two descriptors passed to its base constructor (SpeakerNavigationPopulator.cs:11-31).
    • Depends on: DeclarativeNavigationPopulator<TEntity><Speaker> as its base (SpeakerNavigationPopulator.cs:13), two ChildNavigationDescriptor<TEntity, TParentId, TChild, TChildId> instances closed over SpeakerCategoryItem and SpeakerQuestionAnswer (:15, :22), and IUnitOfWork, which it only forwards (:12-13).
    • Concept introduced: the descriptor mechanism itself is taught in group 11 on DeclarativeNavigationPopulator<TEntity> and ChildNavigationDescriptor<TEntity, TParentId, TChild, TChildId>; this class is the binding, alongside its three siblings EventNavigationPopulator, SessionNavigationPopulator, and ConferenceCategoryNavigationPopulator. What is worth learning here is when it actually fires. The base loops the descriptors and loads one only if its PropertyName appears in navigationMetadata.UnsupportedIncludes (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/Navigation/DeclarativeNavigationPopulator.cs:27-41), and a navigation is classified unsupported only when the parent and child resolve to different physical data sources, or to Cosmos (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/Query/NavigationMetadataProvider.cs:96-99 calling HaveIncludeSupport, defined as first == second && first.Engine != DataSource.CosmosDB at MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Services/DataSourceService.cs:31-32). In ADC today every Conference entity lives in the one ADC_Conference SQL Server database, so both navigations classify as supported, EF Include() handles them, and this populator's loop does nothing. It is standing capacity for a source split, not code on today's hot path (ADR-002, ADR-018). [Rubric §8, Data Architecture] assesses whether the persistence strategy can change without rewriting the layers above: the read path already routes every child load through this abstraction, so moving Speaker to its own source changes classification, not code.
    • Walkthrough: two descriptors, four members each, and both follow the same shape.
      • SpeakerCategoryItems (SpeakerNavigationPopulator.cs:15-21): PropertyName = nameof(Speaker.SpeakerCategoryItems) is the string the base matches against the metadata; ParentKeySelector = e => e.Id extracts the parent key; ChildForeignKeySelector = child => child.SpeakerId is an Expression, not a delegate, because the base builds a WHERE SpeakerId IN (...) predicate out of it; AssignAction = (e, categoryItems) => e.SetSpeakerCategoryItems(categoryItems) hands the grouped results back to the aggregate.
      • SpeakerQuestionAnswers (:22-28): identical apart from the child type, the property name, and the setter.
      • The load itself is one batched query per descriptor: ChildNavigationDescriptor<TEntity, TParentId, TChild, TChildId>.LoadAsync forwards to NavigationLoader.LoadChildrenPropertyAsync, which collects the distinct parent ids, issues a single WHERE ParentFK IN (...) query, groups the rows, and assigns (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/Navigation/ChildNavigationDescriptor.cs:37-47, MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/NavigationLoader.cs:102-106). Two descriptors means at most two extra round-trips for a whole page of speakers, not two per speaker. [Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]: the N+1 is designed out at the loader, so a populator author cannot reintroduce it.
    • Why it's built this way: the assignment goes through the aggregate rather than around it. SetSpeakerCategoryItems and SetSpeakerQuestionAnswers are internal methods on the domain entity (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/Speakers/Speaker.cs:381-382, :458-459) that delegate to the framework's SetItems helper, and the Application project can call them only because the Domain project grants it InternalsVisibleTo (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Domain.csproj:3). The public surface stays read-only: both collections are exposed as IReadOnlyCollection<T> over private backing lists (Speaker.cs:60, :66). [Rubric §4, Domain-Driven Design] and [Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]: an infrastructure concern (batch loading) refills the aggregate without any layer gaining write access to its collections, and the Application layer takes no EF dependency to do it.
    • Where it's used: registered as INavigationPopulator<Speaker> at MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:60, one line above the SpeakerEntityQueryService registration that consumes it (:61). The base query service calls NavigationPopulator.PopulateAsync as part of every pipeline execution (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Services/EntityQueryService.cs:439-444). Covered by SpeakerNavigationPopulatorTests (MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Application.Tests/Speakers/SpeakerNavigationPopulatorTests.cs:9).
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the descriptors name properties and setters as strings and lambdas resolved at construction, so renaming or adding a child collection on Speaker compiles fine here and simply stops that collection from ever being populated in a split-source deployment; nothing in the build fails. The two SpeakerId foreign keys must exist on the child entities for the expression to translate, which is a persistence-model fact this file assumes rather than states.
